name: How much does a gut renovation cost per square foot in Los Angeles right now?

mainEntity.name: What is a realistic cost per square foot for a gut renovation in Los Angeles for mid-range versus luxury finishes?
mainEntity.text: What is a realistic cost per square foot for a gut renovation in Los Angeles for mid-range versus luxury finishes?

acceptedAnswer.text: A realistic Los Angeles gut-renovation budget should be built from scope, not a generic average. Costs usually rise quickly when the project includes moving walls, replacing electrical and plumbing, upgrading HVAC, window or roof changes, and high-end finishes. Mid-range gut renovations often land in the low-to-mid hundreds per square foot, while luxury homes can go substantially higher when custom cabinetry, stone, specialty millwork, and imported fixtures are involved. Older homes also carry bigger risk because once demolition starts, contractors may uncover framing damage, outdated wiring, slab issues, or water intrusion. A good budget should include design fees, permit costs, contingency, and temporary housing if the home becomes uninhabitable. Homeowners should compare bids on the same scope sheet, not just the total price.
acceptedAnswer.description: A gut renovation in Los Angeles commonly costs far more than a cosmetic remodel because it includes demolition, structural work, new systems, permits, and finish replacement. Mid-range projects often start around the low hundreds per square foot, while luxury projects can climb much higher depending on layout changes, custom materials, and hidden conditions.
